ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows an ideal two-winding transformer labeled n:1. The left port is labeled V1 with an upward voltage reference, and its current I1 is drawn entering the top left terminal toward the transformer. The right port is labeled V2 with an upward voltage reference, and its current I2 is drawn entering the top right terminal from the right toward the transformer. Reasoning: From the given ABCD matrix [n 0; 0 x], we identify A = n, B = 0, C = 0, and D = x. For an ideal n:1 transformer with the shown voltage references, V1 = n V2. Since the transformer is ideal and lossless, using the shown current directions entering the ports gives V1 I1 + V2 I2 = 0, so I1 = -I2/n. With the ABCD convention [V1; I1] = [A B; C D][V2; -I2], the current equation is I1 = C V2 + D(-I2) = x(-I2), because C = 0. Comparing this with I1 = -I2/n gives x = 1/n.
